questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power Compared To a Negative Number
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(7-4x)^{2}+5 & <-25 \\ 3(7-4x)^{2} & <-30 \\ (7-4x)^{2} & <-10\end{aligned}
$$

However, $(7-4x)^{2}\ge 0$ for all values of $x$ because the power $(2)$ is even.

Therefore, there is no solution to the given inequality.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-2)^{6}-1 & \ge 3 \\ 2(x-2)^{6} & \ge 4 \\ (x-2)^{6} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(x-2)^{6}} & \ge \sqrt[6]{2} \\ |x-2| & \ge \sqrt[6]{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-2\le -\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x-2\ge \sqrt[6]{2}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x\le 2-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 2+\sqrt[6]{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-6)^{2}+4 & \ge 11 \\ (x-6)^{2} & \ge 7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the square root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(x-6)^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{7} \\ |x-6| & \ge \sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-6\ge \sqrt{7}\,\text{or}\,x-6\le -\sqrt{7}
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}x-6 & \ge \sqrt{7} &  &  & x-6 & \le -\sqrt{7} \\ x & \ge \sqrt{7}+6 &  &  & x & \le -\sqrt{7}+6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
x\le -\sqrt{7}+6\,\text{or}\,x\ge \sqrt{7}+6.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving an Even Power
questions.worked_solution:
Isolating the quartic-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x-5)^{4}-4 & \ge 23 \\ 3(x-5)^{4} & \ge 27 \\ (x-5)^{4} & \ge 9.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the fourth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[4]{(x-5)^{4}} & \ge \sqrt[4]{9} \\ |x-5| & \ge \sqrt[4]{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-5\ge \sqrt[4]{9}\,\text{or}\,x-5\le -\sqrt[4]{9}
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & \ge \sqrt[4]{9} &  &  & x-5 & \le -\sqrt[4]{9} \\ x & \ge \sqrt[4]{9}+5 &  &  & x & \le -\sqrt[4]{9}+5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
x\le -\sqrt[4]{9}+5\,\text{or}\,x\ge \sqrt[4]{9}+5.
$$
